context: Follow-up to the cmux teammate minimal-PATH diagnosis: the plugin bundles the same npx-launched stdio server and fails the same way.
rationale: The hook runs with the same environment Claude Code uses to spawn stdio MCP servers, so `command -v npx` there sees exactly what the server spawn saw — a faithful detector. It converts the silent failure into an actionable in-context warning and stops the gates from demanding tool calls the session cannot make (consistent with the fail-open hook doctrine). Changing the plugin's server command to `sh -lc` would fix POSIX minimal-PATH spawns but risks breaking Windows plugin users: `sh` does not reliably resolve on Windows, static MCP JSON cannot be platform-conditional, and env-var expansion in plugin .mcp.json is broken upstream (anthropics/claude-code#9427). Windows sessions inherit the registry PATH and largely don't hit this failure, so the wrapper's benefit there is nil while its risk is total.
summary: Chose SessionStart-hook detection (warn loudly + suppress gates when npx is unresolvable) over changing plugin/.mcp.json to the sh -lc wrapper
